proof.criterion: Review round 3 D1: a revoked socket in the middle of a large frame closes with 1012, and the page sees 1012, not 1006 or 1002 (including a repeat of the run that once missed).
proof.surface: Real envoy-dispatch processes of this head (cur, fast V3/R3) on one database and one nats-server; real gorilla websocket pages: a victim that does not read until 2 s after the tick, and a writer page in the same room sending 30 x 300 KB paragraph updates
proof.command: d1v2.sh (victim opens at tick-5.2s with -pause 7.2; writer sends from tick-4.7s; the fast build starts at tick-4.9s), 4 trials; small-document runs with the fast build started 1-6s after the socket opened, 8 trials
proof.observed: Large frames: 4 of 4, the page read 6 whole 300 KB messages then CLOSE 1012 'the server processes changed; reconnect'. Loopback capacity measured at about 1.5 MB (a non-reading page's write timed out after 5 x 300 KB), so the server's writer was blocked on the room's next frame at the revoke. Small document: 8 of 8 closed with 1012. With calibration, 13 of 13.
proof.negativeControl: The pre-fix build (b52a1c5d) also closed cleanly with 1012 in the same 6 real-socket trials: this pod's loopback accepts a blocked frame write whole. At b52a1c5d, TestARevokedSocketsCloseFrameWaitsForTheEndOfAMessage FAILs ('read ... 4139 bytes (websocket: close 1006 ...)'); at this head it PASSes 5 of 5.

proof.criterion: Review round 3 D2: a revoked socket's late token never leaves another admitted socket read-only.

proof.command: d2trial.sh: the V3/R2 process stops 2s before a re-check tick; X's token goes out at tick+delta ms and Y's 1 ms later, with delta in {-6,-4,-2,0,3,8,5000}

At b52a1c5d, TestARevokedSocketKeepsItsPlaceUntilItsTokenIsAnswered FAILs ('the second token of the key was answered read-only'); at this head it and ...WhoseTokenWasAnsweredIsForgotten PASS 5 of 5.
